AiMuxError.description:
Unified error type for all aimux operations.

Variants are cut by *what the caller does about it*, not by where the
failure came from. `ApiCallError` is boxed only to keep the Rust enum
compact; serde and every binding still observe the same object shape.

A variant has a `cause` exactly where its AI SDK class takes one; it is
what `source()` returns. `Retry` reports its
last attempt and `ToolCallRepair` its `cause` the same way.

settingName.description: `name` is the union's tag key, so the setting's name is `settingName`.

ApiCallError.description:
What a failed API call observed — the field set of the AI SDK's
`APICallError` (`statusCode` / `responseBody`), which this project's error
taxonomy mirrors (docs/internal/vercel-research/07-kernel-infrastructure.md).

Carried by [`AiMuxError::ApiCall`] alone. There are no per-status
variants: a 401, 404 or 429 is an `ApiCall` error whose classification is
read from `status_code`, exactly as the AI SDK reads
`APICallError.statusCode`. Transport failures (connection reset, DNS,
body read) are `ApiCall` errors too — no response arrived, so
`status_code` is `None` and `is_retryable` is `true`, exactly as the AI
SDK's `handleFetchError` builds an `APICallError` with no `statusCode`
and `isRetryable: true`. `message` holds the provider's text verbatim when
one is available; transport and parsing failures use a library message
with the source detail appended. The HTTP status is always a field, never
baked into the string; `Display` composes the human-readable form from the
fields at print time, so nothing downstream has to parse it back out.

Every producer must provide the sanitized request URL and request values.
This keeps transport and response failures self-contained and matches the
AI SDK's `APICallError` contract.

cause.description:
The error this failure was built from (`APICallError.cause`): the
transport error with its source chain, the body parse error, or the
aimux error a response handler returned.

isRetryable.description:
Whether retrying can help (`APICallError.isRetryable`) — stored at
construction, exactly like the AI SDK: the response path computes it
from the status (408/409/429 or 5xx), and the transport path (no response, so
no status to compute from) sets it to `true` explicitly.

origin.description:
The boundary this error was built at: before a response arrived, from
an HTTP response, from an event inside an accepted stream, or locally.
Not in the AI SDK's `APICallError`: a host deciding whether a retry
could replay output it already delivered cannot tell an HTTP 429 from
an in-stream 429 frame by the status and response body. Omitted from
the JSON when `unknown`, which is also what an error serialized
without the field reads back as.

providerCode.description:
Provider's machine-readable code (OpenAI's `code`/`type`,
e.g. `"rate_limit_exceeded"` vs `"insufficient_quota"`). Never an HTTP
status. Our normalized take on `APICallError.data`.

requestBodyValues.description: Sanitized request values used to create the API request.

responseBody.description:
The raw response body, verbatim (`APICallError.responseBody`) — the
lossless evidence when `message`/`provider_code` are extractions.
`None` when the error did not come from a response body.

statusCode.description:
HTTP status of the response, when it came from one
(`APICallError.statusCode`). The HTTP layer fills the observed status
for every response-derived error. An error frame inside a stream
carries the status its provider maps it to, as upstream's provider
stream errors do (OpenAI infers one from the frame's `code`/`type`,
Anthropic from its error type); errors built without an HTTP exchange
leave it `None`.

url.description: Sanitized request URL. Required for every API-derived failure.

ApiCallErrorOrigin.description:
Where an [`ApiCallError`] was built. Orthogonal to its `cause`, which
says what the underlying error was.

oneOf.description:
No complete response: connecting, sending, or reading the response
body failed (connection refused or reset, DNS, TLS, a broken body
stream, a proxy that refused the tunnel). `status_code` is `None`
unless the body broke after the status line arrived.

Built from an HTTP response before any stream output: a non-2xx
status, a 2xx body that was too large or did not parse, an error the
provider reported in a 2xx body (a failed job when polling), or a
redirect that could not be followed.

Built from an event inside an accepted stream: a provider error frame
(SSE, AWS event stream, WebSocket) or a frame that could not be
decoded. The stream's HTTP status was 2xx; `status_code` is the one
the provider maps the event to.

Built by aimux with no response to point at, such as the exchange
response timeout.

Not recorded: an error deserialized from input that predates the
field, or built by code that did not set it. Never inferred from the
other fields.

returns binary, return [`FileBytes::Binary`].

The JSON is a base64 string either way, as in the AI SDK's JSON: `Binary`
is written as base64 and parsing yields `Base64`. Two values are equal when
they hold the same bytes, whatever their form.

The structured output to generate, the AI SDK's `output`
(`generate-text/output.ts`). It sets the model call's
`response_format` and parses the final text into

takes the text as the output.

Session identifier, for grouping consecutive calls into a session
(observability, see RFC-0024). Orthogonal to RFC-0019 session-affinity

may be inferred from prompt-prefix continuation.

strictStream.description:
Strict stream mode: end the stream with a terminal error when
the protocol's evidence of a complete reply is missing (the stream
ends without its terminal event, a block delta arrives outside a
started block, a block starts twice). Client tool calls are delivered
only right before the finish. Off by default, as in the AI SDK.

GenerateTextResult.description:
Result of `generate_text` and of a consumed `stream_text`: the AI SDK's
`GenerateTextResult` (ai@7.0.127 `generate-text/generate-text-result.ts`).

`DefaultGenerateTextResult` does (`generate-text.ts:1691-1808`); every
other value is derived from the steps by an accessor. The serialized form
is a snapshot that writes the derived values next to the stored ones, so
a binding reads `text`, `tool_calls`, `usage` and the rest directly. Only
`steps`, `total_usage` and `output` are read back.

AiMuxError.description:
Unified error type for all aimux operations.

Variants are cut by *what the caller does about it*, not by where the
failure came from. `ApiCallError` is boxed only to keep the Rust enum
compact; serde and every binding still observe the same object shape.

A variant has a `cause` exactly where its AI SDK class takes one; it is
what `source()` returns. `Retry` reports its
last attempt and `ToolCallRepair` its `cause` the same way.

settingName.description: `name` is the union's tag key, so the setting's name is `settingName`.

ApiCallError.description:
What a failed API call observed — the field set of the AI SDK's
`APICallError` (`statusCode` / `responseBody`), which this project's error
taxonomy mirrors (docs/internal/vercel-research/07-kernel-infrastructure.md).

Carried by [`AiMuxError::ApiCall`] alone. There are no per-status
variants: a 401, 404 or 429 is an `ApiCall` error whose classification is
read from `status_code`, exactly as the AI SDK reads
`APICallError.statusCode`. Transport failures (connection reset, DNS,
body read) are `ApiCall` errors too — no response arrived, so
`status_code` is `None` and `is_retryable` is `true`, exactly as the AI
SDK's `handleFetchError` builds an `APICallError` with no `statusCode`
and `isRetryable: true`. `message` holds the provider's text verbatim when
one is available; transport and parsing failures use a library message
with the source detail appended. The HTTP status is always a field, never
baked into the string; `Display` composes the human-readable form from the
fields at print time, so nothing downstream has to parse it back out.

Every producer must provide the sanitized request URL and request values.
This keeps transport and response failures self-contained and matches the
AI SDK's `APICallError` contract.

cause.description:
The error this failure was built from (`APICallError.cause`): the
transport error with its source chain, the body parse error, or the
aimux error a response handler returned.

isRetryable.description:
Whether retrying can help (`APICallError.isRetryable`) — stored at
construction, exactly like the AI SDK: the response path computes it
from the status (408/409/429 or 5xx), and the transport path (no response, so
no status to compute from) sets it to `true` explicitly.

origin.description:
The boundary this error was built at: before a response arrived, from
an HTTP response, from an event inside an accepted stream, or locally.
Not in the AI SDK's `APICallError`: a host deciding whether a retry
could replay output it already delivered cannot tell an HTTP 429 from
an in-stream 429 frame by the status and response body. Omitted from
the JSON when `unknown`, which is also what an error serialized
without the field reads back as.

providerCode.description:
Provider's machine-readable code (OpenAI's `code`/`type`,
e.g. `"rate_limit_exceeded"` vs `"insufficient_quota"`). Never an HTTP
status. Our normalized take on `APICallError.data`.

requestBodyValues.description: Sanitized request values used to create the API request.

responseBody.description:
The raw response body, verbatim (`APICallError.responseBody`) — the
lossless evidence when `message`/`provider_code` are extractions.
`None` when the error did not come from a response body.

statusCode.description:
HTTP status of the response, when it came from one
(`APICallError.statusCode`). The HTTP layer fills the observed status
for every response-derived error. An error frame inside a stream
carries the status its provider maps it to, as upstream's provider
stream errors do (OpenAI infers one from the frame's `code`/`type`,
Anthropic from its error type); errors built without an HTTP exchange
leave it `None`.

url.description: Sanitized request URL. Required for every API-derived failure.

ApiCallErrorOrigin.description:
Where an [`ApiCallError`] was built. Orthogonal to its `cause`, which
says what the underlying error was.

oneOf.description:
No complete response: connecting, sending, or reading the response
body failed (connection refused or reset, DNS, TLS, a broken body
stream, a proxy that refused the tunnel). `status_code` is `None`
unless the body broke after the status line arrived.

Built from an HTTP response before any stream output: a non-2xx
status, a 2xx body that was too large or did not parse, an error the
provider reported in a 2xx body (a failed job when polling), or a
redirect that could not be followed.

Built from an event inside an accepted stream: a provider error frame
(SSE, AWS event stream, WebSocket) or a frame that could not be
decoded. The stream's HTTP status was 2xx; `status_code` is the one
the provider maps the event to.

Built by aimux with no response to point at, such as the exchange
response timeout.

Not recorded: an error deserialized from input that predates the
field, or built by code that did not set it. Never inferred from the
other fields.

The error another error was built from: the AI SDK's `cause`.

`APICallError`; any other error is a [`SourceError`]. The JSON form is the

Keep the payload open so newer error variants, provider data, and explicit

FileBytes.description:

Providers should pass file data through without unnecessary conversion: if
the upstream API returns base64, return [`FileBytes::Base64`]; if it
returns binary, return [`FileBytes::Binary`].

tokenEstimate.description:

attached (RFC-0015 §4.1: W capped at one block in this mode).

FunctionTool.description: A tool definition passed to the model in `CallOptions.tools`.

Result of the deprecated [`generate_object`]: the AI SDK's
`GenerateObjectResult` (`generate-object/generate-object-result.ts`).

GenerateTextResult.description:
Result of `generate_text` and of a consumed `stream_text`: the AI SDK's
`GenerateTextResult` (ai@7.0.127 `generate-text/generate-text-result.ts`).

It stores the steps, the usage summed over them and the parsed output, as
`DefaultGenerateTextResult` does (`generate-text.ts:1691-1808`); every
other value is derived from the steps by an accessor. The serialized form
is a snapshot that writes the derived values next to the stored ones, so
a binding reads `text`, `tool_calls`, `usage` and the rest directly. Only
`steps`, `total_usage` and `output` are read back.

output.description: Absent when the output was not parsed.

providerMetadata.description: Deprecated upstream: the last step's provider metadata.

reasoning.description: Deprecated upstream: the last step's reasoning.

reasoningText.description: Deprecated upstream: the last step's reasoning text.

response.description: Deprecated upstream: the last step's response.

GeneratedFile.description:
A generated file (`ai` `generate-text/generated-file.ts:10-32`), the
element of the text results' `files`.

Its JSON is `{ base64, mediaType, providerMetadata? }`: the AI SDK's
`GeneratedFile` exposes the bytes as `base64` and as `uint8Array`, and the
JSON carries them once, as the base64 string. Text generation downloads a
provider's URL file before it builds one (`resolve-generated-file-data.ts`).

base64.description: The file's bytes, `base64` in the JSON.

GeneratedFileData.description: Data or a URL returned for a generated file.

GeneratedFileOutput.description:
A file part of text generation, `{ file, providerMetadata? }` under the
`file` or `reasoning-file` tag (`ai`
`generate-text/convert-language-model-content.ts:55-70`,
`stream-language-model-call.ts:569-590`). The part carries the provider
metadata; the file itself has none.

HandleId.description: Global scope is 0; live resource identifiers are never reused.

HttpExchange.description: ③ HTTP 侧:单次 attempt 的 wire 交换。

attempt.description:
Core operation attempt, starting at 1. Attempt numbers are unique
across the whole call, including composite child steps, so
`(attempt, exchange_index)` alone still identifies an exchange.

exchangeIndex.description: HTTP exchange within the operation attempt, starting at 1.

finalized.description: 流式:该 exchange 是否已终结(收到 response 补全)。非流式恒 true。

response.description: None = 请求失败未获响应。

step.description:
Composite step this exchange belongs to (e.g. `router[0]:openai/gpt-4o`
or `moa.ref[1]:...`). `None` for a plain, non-composite operation.

headers.description: 敏感头(authorization/cookie/含 api-key/key/x-amz-security-token 等)已脱敏为 "\[REDACTED\]"。

The generated images, returned as a homogeneous collection.

The TS result type is `Array<string> | Array<Uint8Array>` — i.e. either all
base64 strings or all binary blobs, never mixed. This enum models that
union. Providers should return data without unnecessary conversion: if the
upstream API returns base64, return [`ImageOutputs::Base64`]; if binary,
return [`ImageOutputs::Binary`].

The JSON is an array of base64 strings either way, as in the AI SDK's
JSON; parsing yields `Base64`.

ImageResponse.description: Response information for an image generation call.

tool's `supportsDeferredResults` (provider-utils@5.0.55

TextStreamPart.description:
A public call-layer stream chunk: the AI SDK's `TextStreamPart`
(ai@7.0.127 `generate-text/stream-text-result.ts:581-607`).

`stream_text` turns the provider's [`StreamPart`]s into these: tool calls
are parsed, text and reasoning deltas carry `text` (the provider part's
`delta`), the provider's `stream-start` and `response-metadata` become
`StartStep` and the `FinishStep` response, and the call is framed by
`Start` ... `Finish`. A provider's tool result becomes `ToolResult` or,
when it reports an error, `ToolError`, both carrying the input of the call
they answer; an invalid client tool call is followed by a `ToolError`
(`stream-language-model-call.ts:709-725`, `:760-792`).

aimux's stream does not produce them yet. Upstream answers approvals and
reports denied tools when it executes tools (`execute-tools-from-stream.ts`
`:170-210`), which aimux does not, and reports the approvals denied in the
prompt's last tool message, provider-executed ones included, before the
first model call (`stream-text.ts:2030-2090`), which needs the prompt's
approval collection (`collect-tool-approvals.ts`), not ported.

Timestamp.description:
A point in time: a `Date` in the AI SDK, whose JSON is
`Date.prototype.toISOString()` (`2024-03-01T12:00:00.000Z`).

It holds a UTC time at millisecond precision, as a JavaScript `Date` does,
in the years 0000 to 9999 that `toISOString` writes in four digits.
Serializing writes that form; parsing reads any RFC 3339 date-time (any
offset, any fraction) and fails on anything else. Parsing and writing back
therefore gives `new Date(text).toISOString()`.
